children: Target (TGT) shares gained after HSBC moved the company to Buy from Hold and lifted its price target to $190 from $125.

The upgrade came after Target's second-quarter performance showed stronger customer activity. Comparable sales increased 3.8%, while profit and earnings per share excluding a $994 million tariff-refund benefit were about 5% above market expectations, HSBC analyst Joe Thomas said.

Thomas pointed to store traffic as a key factor behind the improvement. Average spending per transaction did not drive the increase, suggesting the retailer may be attracting more shoppers rather than relying on larger purchases.

Several categories also recorded progress, including Beauty, Food and Beverage, Hardlines and Household Essentials. Apparel and Home remained weaker areas and could require additional improvement to support a broader recovery.

HSBC now expects fiscal 2027 earnings per share of $10.61, up from $8.26 previously. The bank said better sales could create operating leverage and help margins approach 6% or potentially move higher as the recovery develops.

title: Target Stock Just Got a Stunning Upgrade From HSBC
